text.p: Norwegian pharmaceuticals group Nycomed ASA said on Thursday it had implemented a programme for reducing costs and strengthening core activities.
Focus '98 involves adjusting the company's strategy to reduce costs in some areas and increase investment in other areas.
The company expects to achieve cost savings of about 600 million crowns ($94.1 million) before taxes, to be fully effective from 1998, Nycomed said.

Earlier the company reported a 32 percent fall in 1996 nine-month pre-tax profit to 898 million Norwegian crowns from 1.32 billion in the nine months to September 30, 1995. ($ = 6.376 Norwegian Crowns)

"In the short term, the aim of Focus '98 is to lessen the effect of the price fall in the American market, which will have full impact on earnings in the second half of 1996, as well as to offset expected increased costs from the launch of new therapeutic products," a company statement said.

Focus '98 entails savings of NOK 150-170 million in production, NOK 110-140 million in marketing and sales, NOK 40-60 million in administrative services, NOK 180 million in R&D and NOK 60-80 million in the U.S. operations, Nycomed said.
The programme will not interfere with the continuation of innovative research in medical imaging, it said.
As part of the programme the company will reduce the workforce by 600-700 employees.
Nycomed said between 50 and 70 percent of the anticipated savings were expected to be achieved in the accounting year 1997 with the full effect visible in 1998.
Nycomed said Focus '98 was expected to lead to accrued costs of about 700 million crowns, of which writedowns of balance sheet items and restructuring costs would account for about 50 percent each.
The company took costs of 14 million crowns in its third quarter accounts for measures implemented in the first half of 1996.
